primitives.verbatim_quote: It therefore stands that we should be able to measure if a defender forces an attacker to change their mind or to prevent an attacker from even becoming an option.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'D_{\\text{disrupt}}': 'dimensionless defensive disruption score', 'P_{\\text{pass}}(v)': 'probability of pass completion to vertex v', 'T_{\\text{threat}}(v)': 'threat value of vertex v'}
primitives.assumptions: Players' movements are modeled as stochastic processes; pass probabilities are conditionally independent given game state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When pass completion likelihood exceeds threshold T = 0.7, disruption is considered negligible.

primitives.name: Off-Ball Threat Surface
primitives.verbatim_quote: Given enough data, we should be able to predict where a player will pass the ball, the likelihood of that pass being completed and whether this pass will result in a scoring opportunity.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{T}(v)': 'threat surface at vertex v', 'x\\text{Threat}': 'expected threat of shot in next 10s'}
primitives.assumptions: Threat surface is a deterministic function of player positions and movement dynamics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Surface becomes undefined when positional data is missing or corrupted beyond interpolation bounds.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphically maps off-ball positioning to threat probability using graph-based spatial convolution.
layer2.telemetry: Change in threat surface entropy during active possession.

primitives.name: Player Availability Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: Virgil Van Dijk is considered one of the best defenders in world soccer as he has the ability to prevent a pass being made to an open attacker to shoot by forcing the ball carrier to pass somewhere else less dangerous.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{A}(v)': 'availability of player v', '\\mathcal{N}(v)': 'set of neighbors of v', 'P_{\\text{pass}}(u,v)': 'probability of pass from u to v'}
primitives.assumptions: Availability is inversely correlated with opponent proximity and directly proportional to pass completion likelihood.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Metric becomes invalid when neighbor set is empty or pass probabilities are undefined.

layer2.mapping: Derives availability from xPass and xReceiver outputs to quantify defensive suppression of offensive options.
layer2.telemetry: Reduction in average pass completion rate to available targets.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that traditional metrics like tackles and interceptions fail to capture preventive defensive behavior. The paper introduces a graph convolutional network to model player interactions dynamically. Each player and the ball form nodes in a directed graph, with edges representing potential passes. The model computes xPass, xReceiver, and xThreat, enabling prediction of future actions. The Defensive Disruption Index measures how much a defender alters offensive decision-making by changing pass probabilities. Off-Ball Threat Surface models the danger posed by each player's position, integrating xThreat and xPass. Player Availability Metric evaluates how effectively a defender suppresses nearby attackers' pass options. All primitives are grounded in graph theory and probabilistic modeling, allowing for dynamic, real-time assessment of defensive performance.
